title: Shishupala Incites the Kings to Battle
story:
Krishna had received the first worship of the Rajasuya, and the great hall of Indraprastha changed in a single breath from a place of ceremony into a place of war. The kings of the earth had come to Yudhishthira's sacrifice from every direction, to witness the rite, to share in its glory, to be counted among its guests. And when the first offering of honor went to Krishna, before any of them, the assembly had felt the sting of it. They had carried that sting through the long rites, and the air of the hall had grown thick with it.

Then Shishupala, king of Chedi, rose and gave the anger a voice. "When I am here to head you all," he cried out, "what are you thinking of now? Arrayed, let us stand in battle against the assembled Vrishnis and the Pandavas!"

The words found their mark at once. The vast assembly of kings, already agitated with wrath, stirred like the terrific sea when the winds that blow at the time of universal dissolution whip it into frenzy. All around the hall, the countless waves of troops that had ridden in with their masters seemed to gather themselves for a rush. It was the moment the ceremonies had been building toward without anyone daring to name it.

Krishna saw it before anyone else. Seated in his place, he understood that the vast sea of monarchs, with its countless waves of troops, was preparing for a terrific rush, and he did not move. He neither rose nor reached for a weapon nor called for his chariot. He waited, as a man waits when he has already seen the end of a thing.

Yudhishthira saw the same storm and read it differently. This was his sacrifice, his city, his guests, and the ruin of any one of them would be his. He leaned toward Bhishma, the grandsire of the Kurus, who sat near him like a mountain among men. "This vast ocean of kings has been agitated by wrath," he said. "Tell me, O Grandsire, what I should do, so that my sacrifice may not be obstructed and my subjects may not be injured."

Bhishma answered as though the matter were already settled. "Fear not, O tiger of the Kurus. Can the dog slay the lion? As dogs in a pack approach the lion that is asleep and bark together, so are all these lords of earth. Before the sleeping lion of the Vrishni race, these monarchs are only barking in rage. Achyuta now is like a lion asleep. Until he wakes, this chief of the Chedis makes these monarchs look like lions."

The old man's voice did not rise, and the hall leaned in to hear him. "This Shishupala, possessed of little intelligence, is desirous of taking all these kings along with him, through the agency of him who is the soul of the universe, to the regions of Yama. Assuredly, Vishnu has been desirous of taking back unto himself the energy that exists in this Shishupala. The intelligence of this wicked-minded king of the Chedis, as also of all these monarchs, has become perverse. Indeed, the intelligence of all those whom this tiger among men desires to take unto himself becomes perverse, even like that of the king of the Chedis. O Yudhishthira, Madhava is the progenitor as also the destroyer of all created beings of the four species existing in the three worlds."

He fell silent, and the silence was heavier than the shouting had been. Kings glanced at one another, uncertain whether the rage they felt was their own or something placed in them.

But the ruler of Chedis had heard every word, and it had not cooled him. He turned on the grandsire, and when he spoke, his words were stern and rough, the words of a man who means to answer a prophecy with a war.
reflection: Bhishma's calm before a hall of furious kings is not a dismissal of their numbers; it is a reading of their anger as a prelude. The more the monarchs rage, the closer he knows the end to be — the fury of the hall is not the danger but the sign.
next_story_tease: Shishupala, however, had heard every word — and his answer was already forming on his lips.
hero_scene: Inside the great hall of Indraprastha: Krishna seated, utterly still, while a sea of furious kings surges around him — Shishupala on his feet, arm raised toward the throng, as Yudhishthira leans toward white-haired Bhishma for counsel.
visual_elements: the vast assembly of kings stirred like a storm-tossed sea
Shishupala standing, calling the monarchs to battle
Krishna seated unmoved, reading the oncoming rush
Yudhishthira leaning to Bhishma in the midst of the uproar
countless waves of troops gathering around the hall
